description: Query-string parameters accepted by app.diagrams.net, viewer.diagrams.net and embed.diagrams.net (and by the desktop app's internal URL through configuration). They select the UI theme and language, hide chrome, enable the read-only lightbox viewer, choose storage back ends, preload libraries and plugins, and switch on embed mode. Content itself is passed through hash properties (#R, #U, #H, #G, #W, #L, #A, #D) so it never reaches the server.

tools.name: ?lightbox=1
tools.description: Opens the diagram in the read-only lightbox viewer: no menus or sidebar, a floating toolbar with zoom, page and layer controls, and an Edit button when edit= is set. It is the mode used by File > Publish > Link and by the HTML embed's 'open in lightbox'. Combine with nav=1, layers=1, highlight= and page= for interactive read-only diagrams.
tools.notes: hide-pages=1, border=, transparent=1, toolbar=0, close=1 and target= only apply in lightbox/chromeless mode. viewer.diagrams.net is a viewer-only deployment; app.diagrams.net accepts the same parameters.

tools.name: ?chrome=0
tools.description: Runs the editor as a chromeless read-only viewer without the lightbox overlay: menus, sidebar and format panel are removed and the diagram fills the window. lightbox=1 is the usual choice; chrome=0 alone is what File > Embed > IFrame and the HTML viewer use internally.
tools.notes: Interaction (links, folding, layers, tooltips) still works. Use toolbar=0 to also remove the viewer toolbar.

tools.name: ?highlight=RRGGBB
tools.description: Colour used in chromeless/lightbox mode to outline cells that carry a link when the mouse hovers over them, so viewers can discover clickable shapes. The value is a hex colour without the leading #.
tools.notes: Corresponds to the highlight key of the HTML viewer's data-mxgraph JSON. Set link-icons=1 to always show an icon on linked cells instead of relying on hover.

tools.name: ?edit=url|_blank
tools.description: Adds an Edit button to the lightbox toolbar. edit=_blank opens a copy of the diagram in a new editor tab (the viewer's content is duplicated, not linked back); any other URL is opened as-is, so a host application can point it to its own edit page.

parameters.name: _blank
parameters.description: Open a new editor with a copy of the diagram.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Custom URL-encoded link for the Edit button.

tools.notes: Mirrors the edit key of the HTML viewer configuration.

tools.name: ?nav=1
tools.description: Enables folding (collapse/expand of containers and tree nodes) in chromeless and lightbox mode, which is otherwise disabled to keep viewers static. Required for interactive read-only diagrams that rely on collapsible containers.
tools.notes: Same as the nav key of the HTML viewer JSON. Folding state is not persisted.

tools.name: ?layers=1 / ?layer-ids= / ?tags=
tools.description: layers=1 adds a layer-visibility control to the chromeless/lightbox toolbar; layer-ids=id1%20id2 (space-separated, URL-encoded) shows only the listed layer ids at start; tags=<json> preselects tag visibility for diagrams that use tags. All three let a single diagram serve several audiences with one link.

parameters.name: layer-ids
parameters.description: Space-separated layer cell ids to make visible.

tools.notes: Layer ids are the mxCell ids of the layer cells under root (the default layer is id 1).

tools.name: ?target=auto|self|frame|blank
tools.description: Where links inside a chromeless/lightbox diagram open: auto (default, page links in place and external links in a new window), self (same window), frame (the parent frame) or blank (new window). Set it to match the embedding context, for example self when the diagram acts as an in-page menu.
tools.notes: The HTML viewer uses the target key with the same values.

tools.name: ?toolbar=0 / ?toolbar-config= / ?noPrint=1 / ?noExport=1 / ?close=1
tools.description: Toolbar controls for chromeless/lightbox mode: toolbar=0 removes the toolbar entirely, toolbar-config=<url-encoded JSON> configures which buttons appear, noPrint=1 and noExport=1 hide the print and image-export buttons, and close=1 adds a Close button that sends an exit message to an embedding host.
tools.notes: For the HTML viewer the equivalent is the toolbar key ('pages zoom layers lightbox').

tools.name: ?border= / ?transparent=1 (lightbox)
tools.description: Appearance of the lightbox canvas: border=<px> sets the margin around the diagram (default 60) and transparent=1 removes the white page background so the host page shows through. Both are cosmetic and apply only in chromeless/lightbox mode.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: Margin in px around the diagram.

tools.notes: For exported images use the export dialog's Border and Transparent options instead.

tools.name: ?title= / ?notitle=1 / ?template-filename=
tools.description: Naming of a diagram loaded or created from the URL: title=<name> sets the file title used with create= or a #U hash (and shown in the lightbox toolbar); notitle=1 keeps the default filename when opening from a URL; template-filename=<name> supplies the filename for binary (.png/.svg) content loaded via #U.

parameters.name: notitle
parameters.description: 1 uses the default name for URL-loaded files.

parameters.name: template-filename
parameters.description: Filename applied to binary content from #U.

tools.notes: The title becomes the suggested filename on Save As.

tools.name: ?open=<prefix><id>
tools.description: Opens a file by storage prefix and id as an alternative to hash properties, e.g. open=G<driveId>, open=W<onedrive>, open=H<github path>, open=U<url>, open=R<xml>. Useful when the URL is generated by a system that cannot emit a fragment, or when the fragment is reserved by the host page.
tools.usage: ?open=G1a2b3c   (same prefixes as the hash: R, U, G, W, H, A, D, L)

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Storage letter: R raw XML, U URL, G Google Drive, W OneDrive, H GitHub, A GitLab, D Dropbox, L browser storage.

tools.notes: Unlike the hash, query parameters are sent to the server in the request line, so prefer #U/#R for private content.

tools.name: ?create=url|{json} / ?smart-template=
tools.description: Creates a new diagram on load. create=<url> uses the file at the URL as a template; create=<url-encoded JSON> with {"type":"xml"|"csv"|"mermaid"|"generate"|"message","data":"..."} builds the diagram from XML, CSV-import text, Mermaid source or an AI prompt, optionally with "layout" (preset name or layout array) and "applyLayouts":true. smart-template=<prompt> is a shortcut for an AI-generated diagram from text.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: xml, csv, mermaid, generate or message.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The content in the given type.

parameters.name: layout / applyLayouts
parameters.description: Optional layout preset or array; applyLayouts=true runs layouts stored in the diagram.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Combine with ?title= to name the new file.

tools.notes: The JSON must be URL-encoded once; newlines inside data become %5Cn. generate/message types need the AI features enabled.

tools.name: ?splash=0
tools.description: Skips the start screen (storage chooser and 'Create New / Open Existing' dialog) so the editor opens directly on a blank diagram or on the content given in the hash. Nearly every generated link uses it.

parameters.description: Do not show the splash/start dialog.

tools.notes: The configuration key showSplashOnStart controls the same dialog for installed configurations.

tools.name: ?ui=kennedy|min|atlas|dark|sketch|simple
tools.description: Selects the editor theme/layout: kennedy (classic default with menus), min (minimal floating panels), atlas (Confluence style), dark (classic in dark colours), sketch (whiteboard style with rough shapes) and simple (the current streamlined UI). The same choice is available under Extras > Theme and is remembered per browser unless the parameter forces it.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Minimal UI with floating shape/format windows.

parameters.name: dark
parameters.description: Classic UI in dark mode (prefer dark=1 with another theme).

parameters.name: sketch
parameters.description: Whiteboard UI; enables sketch style for new shapes.

tools.notes: Embed hosts use ui=min or ui=simple most often. The configuration key ui sets the default for Confluence Cloud.

tools.name: ?dark=0|1|auto / ?high-contrast=1
tools.description: dark=1 forces dark mode, dark=0 light mode and dark=auto follows the operating system preference; high-contrast=1 switches on the high-contrast palette for accessibility. These override the Extras > Appearance setting for the session and are commonly used by embedding pages to match their own theme.
tools.notes: Cells using fillColor=default / strokeColor=default adapt automatically; fixed colours do not. The embed load action also accepts a dark field.

tools.name: ?sketch=0|1 / ?rough=0|1
tools.description: sketch=1 enables the sketch/whiteboard style (rough rendering and the sketch-flavoured UI behaviour) for the session, sketch=0 disables it even in the sketch theme; rough=0|1 controls only whether the hand-drawn rendering is applied to new shapes. Use them when the theme is chosen elsewhere but the drawing style must be fixed.
tools.notes: Existing cells keep their own sketch=1/0 style keys regardless of these parameters.

tools.name: ?lang=xy / ?diagram-language= / ?translate-diagram=1
tools.description: lang=xy sets the UI language (two-letter or locale code such as en, de, fr, es, ja, zh, pt-br); diagram-language=xy selects which language variant of multilingual labels (attributes name_de, name_fr, ...) placeholders resolve; translate-diagram=1 enables that per-language label substitution. browser-translate=0 stops the editor from mirroring text for browser translation tools.

parameters.name: diagram-language
parameters.description: Language suffix used when resolving translated attributes.

tools.notes: Extras > Language changes the same setting interactively; the Docker image's DRAWIO_LANG sets a server default.

tools.name: ?offline=1 / ?pwa=0
tools.description: offline=1 registers the progressive-web-app service worker so app.diagrams.net keeps working without a network connection (offline=0 unregisters it); pwa=0 disables the ability to register the PWA at all. The offline mode disables features that need external services, similar to stealth=1.

parameters.name: offline
parameters.description: 1 install / 0 remove the offline service worker.

tools.notes: The desktop application is always offline; this parameter is for the browser version.

tools.name: ?libs=key1;key2 / ?search-shapes=
tools.description: libs= lists the built-in shape libraries to show in the sidebar, separated by semicolons, using the library keys from the More Shapes dialog (general, uml, uml25, er, bpmn2, flowchart, basic, arrows2, aws4, azure2, gcp2, kubernetes, cisco19, c4, archimate3, sysml, electrical, mockups, ...). search-shapes=<text> preloads the sidebar's search box with a query.

parameters.name: libs
parameters.description: Semicolon-separated library keys; order is preserved.

tools.notes: The configuration keys defaultLibraries and enabledLibraries set the same thing permanently; libs= overrides them for the session.

tools.name: ?clibs=U<url>;...
tools.description: Loads custom shape libraries (.xml files in mxlibrary format) into the sidebar from URLs or storage ids: each entry is a prefix plus an id, e.g. U<url-encoded URL>, G<Google Drive id>, H<GitHub path>. It is how File > Publish > Link shares a diagram together with its libraries and how teams distribute a common stencil set.

parameters.name: U<url>
parameters.description: Library fetched from a URL (server must allow CORS).

parameters.name: G<id> / H<path> / W<id>
parameters.description: Library from Google Drive, GitHub or OneDrive.

tools.notes: The configuration key defaultCustomLibraries does the same for an installed configuration; libraries opened this way appear in the sidebar with a close button.

tools.name: ?configure=1
tools.description: In embed mode, makes the editor send a configure event immediately after loading and wait for the host's configure action (a JSON configuration object) before initialising, so the host can set fonts, colours, libraries and default styles per user. Without it the configuration must come from local storage or the server config.

parameters.description: Request configuration from the host via postMessage.

tools.notes: The init event follows once the configure action has been received.

tools.name: ?embed=1 / ?embedInline=1 / ?client=1
tools.description: embed=1 switches on embed mode, in which the editor has no storage of its own and exchanges diagrams with the host page through postMessage; it is the mandatory parameter for embed.diagrams.net integrations. embedInline=1 configures the inline (in-page, non-modal) variant and implies embed=1, ui=sketch, plugins=0, proto=json and prefetchFonts=1. client=1 runs in client mode with the normal UI while still talking to a host.

parameters.name: embedInline
parameters.description: 1 enables inline embed mode with its presets.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: 1 client mode with the full UI.

tools.notes: Storage-related parameters (mode=, gapi=, od=, ...) are irrelevant in embed mode; ms365 is disabled there by default.

tools.name: ?proto=json / ?spin=1 / ?ready=
tools.description: proto=json selects the JSON postMessage protocol for embed mode (messages are JSON strings with an action/event field) instead of the legacy raw-XML protocol; spin=1 (or spin=<message>) shows a spinner until the host sends the load action; ready=<message> sends that string as the ready message instead of the init event. Almost all integrations use proto=json.

parameters.name: spin
parameters.description: 1 or a custom spinner message shown until load.

tools.notes: Without proto=json the editor expects the host to post the raw XML string and replies with XML, which is deprecated.

tools.name: ?modified=unsavedChanges / ?keepmodified=1
tools.description: Embed-mode status handling: modified=<resourceKey> (for example modified=unsavedChanges) shows that translated message in the editor's status bar whenever the diagram has unsaved changes, and modified=0 suppresses the modified indicator; keepmodified=1 keeps the modified flag set after an autosave so the host decides when changes count as saved.

parameters.name: modified
parameters.description: 0 or a resource key of the message to show.

parameters.name: keepmodified
parameters.description: 1 keeps the modified state after autosave.

tools.notes: The load action's modified field and the status action can change the message at run time.

tools.name: ?saveAndExit=1 / ?noSaveBtn=1 / ?noExitBtn=1 / ?returnbounds=1
tools.description: Embed toolbar and result options: saveAndExit=1 replaces Save with a Save & Exit button (the save event carries exit:true); noSaveBtn=1 removes the Save button (hosts using autosave); noExitBtn=1 removes the Exit button; returnbounds=1 adds the diagram bounds to load/save/export messages so the host can size its preview.

parameters.name: saveAndExit
parameters.description: 1 shows a combined Save & Exit button.

tools.notes: The same flags can be passed per document in the load action (saveAndExit, noSaveBtn, noExitBtn).

tools.name: ?libraries=1 / ?themes=1 (embed)
tools.description: In embed mode the sidebar's custom-library features (New Library, Open Library, Scratchpad) and the Extras > Theme submenu are hidden by default; libraries=1 re-enables the custom library functions and themes=1 shows the theme submenu. Enable them when the host application allows users to manage their own stencils.

parameters.name: libraries
parameters.description: 1 enables custom libraries and the scratchpad in embed mode.

tools.notes: Libraries created in embed mode are stored in the browser unless the host handles the openLink/save flow.

tools.name: ?p=id1;id2 / ?plugins=0
tools.description: p= loads built-in plugins by id for the session (ex, svgdata, number, sql, props, text, anim, update, trees, replay, anon, webcola, tags), separated by semicolons; plugins=0 prevents any plugin from loading, including those stored by the user. Plugins only run in the web app and self-hosted Docker deployments.
tools.notes: Plugins from external URLs must be added through Extras > Plugins, which asks for confirmation; they cannot be injected via p=.

tools.name: ?grid=0|1 / ?pv=0|1 / ?ruler=1 / ?sb=0
tools.description: Canvas view defaults for the session: grid=0 hides the grid (grid=1 forces it), pv=0 disables page view (infinite canvas) while pv=1 shows the page outline, ruler=1 turns on the rulers, and sb=0 starts without scrollbars. The diagram's own mxGraphModel attributes (grid, page) take precedence when a file is loaded.
tools.notes: Configuration keys defaultGridEnabled and defaultPageVisible give installation-wide defaults.

tools.name: ?math=0 / ?math-output=html / ?math-font=
tools.description: MathJax controls: math=0 disables mathematical typesetting support entirely (faster load, no LaTeX/AsciiMath rendering); math-output=html switches MathJax to HTML-CSS output, which makes equations selectable in some PDF exports; math-font=STIX-Web (SVG output) or STIX (HTML-CSS) selects the math font.

parameters.name: math-output
parameters.description: html for HTML-CSS output (default is SVG).

tools.notes: Typesetting itself is switched on per diagram with Extras > Mathematical Typesetting (mxGraphModel math="1").

tools.name: ?pages=0 / ?page=N / ?page-id= / ?hide-pages=1
tools.description: Page handling: page=N opens the diagram at the zero-based page index, page-id=<diagram id> selects a page by its id attribute (takes precedence and survives reordering), pages=0 disables multi-page support (single-page mode), and hide-pages=1 hides the page tabs/controls in lightbox mode so viewers see only the chosen page.

parameters.name: hide-pages
parameters.description: 1 hides page controls in lightbox mode.

tools.notes: Links inside a diagram can also target pages with data:page/id,<id>.

tools.name: ?stealth=1 / ?lockdown=1 / ?gapi-stealth=1
tools.description: Privacy modes: stealth=1 disables every feature that would contact an external service (image proxy, PlantUML, cloud storage, fonts), lockdown=1 blocks all data transmission except to the chosen storage location, and gapi-stealth=1 is stealth with Google Drive still allowed. Use them for confidential diagrams in the browser version; the desktop app behaves this way by default.

parameters.name: lockdown
parameters.description: 1 prevents data transmission except to storage.

tools.notes: The configuration key lockdown gives the same behaviour for an installation.

tools.name: ?gapi=0, ?db=0, ?od=0, ?gh=0, ?gl=0, ?tr=0, ?ms365=0, ?demo=1
tools.description: Toggle individual storage integrations off: gapi (Google Drive), db (Dropbox), od (OneDrive), gh (GitHub), gl (GitLab), tr (Trello) and ms365 (Microsoft 365, disabled by default in embed mode). demo=1 is a shortcut for db=0&gapi=0&math=0&picker=0, giving a local-only demo instance. drive=0 makes the app behave like app.diagrams.net regardless of the domain it is served from.

parameters.name: gapi / db / od / gh / gl / tr / ms365
parameters.description: 0 disables that integration and hides it from dialogs.

tools.notes: Self-hosted Docker deployments disable the integrations whose OAuth environment variables are unset.

tools.name: ?mode=google|onedrive|github|dropbox|gitlab|device|browser|trello
tools.description: Preselects the storage mode so the Open/Save dialogs default to that back end and the start screen is skipped for it. mode=device uses local files, mode=browser the browser's local storage, the others the respective cloud service. sync=none|manual|auto (default auto) controls collaborative sync for Drive/OneDrive files.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: google, onedrive, github, dropbox, gitlab, device, browser or trello.

parameters.name: sync
parameters.description: none, manual or auto for real-time collaboration.

tools.notes: The hash prefix (#H, #G, #W, #D, #A) already implies the mode when opening a specific file.

tools.name: ?local=1 / ?storage=device / ?noDevice=1 / ?browser=0|1 / ?save=local|remote / ?drafts=0
tools.description: Local-storage behaviour: local=1 restricts the app to device mode (no cloud options), storage=device adds the device option on touch devices, noDevice=1 hides device/local file options, browser=0 hides browser storage while browser=1 shows it, save=local or save=remote enables or disables saving to the local file system, and drafts=0 stops the editor from keeping IndexedDB drafts of unsaved diagrams.

parameters.name: storage
parameters.description: device adds local files on touch devices.

tools.notes: Drafts are what the 'Unsaved changes found' recovery dialog restores; disable them on shared kiosks.

tools.name: ?viewbox={...}
tools.description: Opens the diagram scrolled and zoomed to a rectangle given as URL-encoded JSON {"x":int,"y":int,"width":int,"height":int,"border":int} in diagram coordinates, so a link can focus on one region of a large diagram. The embed protocol offers the same through the viewbox action.
tools.notes: Custom links inside a diagram can do the same with the viewbox action.

tools.name: ?vars={json} / ?base=url
tools.description: vars=<url-encoded JSON> defines global placeholder variables (e.g. {"env":"prod"}) that %env% resolves to in labels, tooltips and links, letting one diagram render differently per link; base=<url> sets the base URL against which relative links in the diagram are resolved.

parameters.name: vars
parameters.description: JSON object of placeholder name/value pairs.

tools.notes: The configuration key globalVars supplies the same variables permanently; cell-level attributes override both.

tools.name: ?format=0 / ?sidebar=0 / ?sidebar-entries=large / ?windows=0 / ?shape-picker=0 / ?touch=1
tools.description: Chrome tweaks for the editor: format=0 hides the Format panel, sidebar=0 hides the shape sidebar, sidebar-entries=large enlarges sidebar thumbnails, windows=0 disables floating windows (min/sketch themes), shape-picker=0 disables the quick shape picker that appears when clicking hover arrows or double-clicking the canvas, and touch=1 forces the touch interface (android=0|1 overrides Android detection).
tools.notes: Ctrl+Shift+P and Ctrl+Shift+K still toggle the panels unless the host also uses hideMenus/hideMenuItems in the configuration.

tools.name: ?picker=0 / ?thumb=0 / ?gitlab= / ?gitlab-id= / ?rev=
tools.description: Cloud-specific switches: picker=0 disables the Google file picker in dialogs, thumb=0 stops draw.io from writing Drive thumbnails, gitlab=<url> and gitlab-id=<client id> point the GitLab integration at a self-hosted instance and OAuth application, and rev=<id> opens a specific revision of a Google Drive or Dropbox file.

parameters.name: gitlab / gitlab-id
parameters.description: Custom GitLab base URL and OAuth client id.

tools.notes: For a permanent self-hosted GitLab setup use the Docker variables DRAWIO_GITLAB_URL and DRAWIO_GITLAB_ID instead.

tools.name: ?nowarn=1 / ?svg-warning=0 / ?openInSameWin=1 / ?suppressNewWindows=1
tools.description: Window and warning behaviour: nowarn=1 suppresses the 'unsaved changes' unload prompt for local files, svg-warning=0 hides the warning about SVG output in older viewers, openInSameWin=1 opens files in the current window instead of new tabs, and suppressNewWindows=1 routes link clicks through the embedding host (openLink event) rather than opening windows itself.

parameters.name: openInSameWin
parameters.description: 1 reuses the window when opening files.

parameters.name: suppressNewWindows
parameters.description: 1 delegates link opening to the host.

tools.notes: suppressNewWindows is also available as a configuration key.

tools.name: ?link-icons=1 / ?tooltip-icons=1 / ?tooltips=0
tools.description: Viewer affordances: link-icons=1 draws a small overlay icon on every cell that has a link, tooltip-icons=1 does the same for cells with tooltips, and tooltips=0 suppresses cell tooltips altogether in the viewer. They make interactive read-only diagrams discoverable without hover.
tools.notes: Configuration keys showLinkIcons and showTooltipIcons set the same defaults; the HTML viewer uses show-link-icons / show-tooltip-icons.
